source.title: On a continuous time model of gradient descent dynamics and instability in deep learning
source.authors: Mihaela Rosca; Yan Wu; C. Qin; Benoit Dherin

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures training loss and Hessian behavior in neural-network gradient descent to examine instability near the learning-rate stability threshold. This is a conceptual test of V5, though it does not test all of that version's stated settings or outcomes.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own gradient-descent results on loss increases and the Hessian threshold. Statements about Cohen et al. (2021) and Lewkowycz et al. (2020) are cited prior work and are not recorded as this study's results. Figures 9, 12, and 13 provide no exact numerical values in the text, so the rows use figure_only values.
record.test_reason: The study independently measures training loss and largest Hessian eigenvalues during full-batch gradient descent, directly testing V5's edge-of-stability component with the same core method and measures. Its principal-flow analysis adds an explanation of those observations.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that their complex-valued principal flow better captures gradient-descent oscillations and instability, exposes stability coefficients beyond sharpness alone, and motivates DAL learning-rate adaptation. They also report a trade-off connecting greater discretization drift with improved generalization and reduced training stability.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes gradient-descent dynamics using a proposed continuous-time principal flow and empirical measurements of Hessian eigenvalues, loss, and stability coefficients; it does not reproduce the specific training recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported instability behavior is considered across learning rates, datasets, and architectures; the text highlights the dependence on whether λ0 exceeds 2/h and on the leading-direction stability coefficient.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss-increase peaks align with peaks in a gradient-normalized principal-flow stability coefficient.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient alignment with the leading Hessian eigendirection helps explain the timing and strength of training instabilities.

record.problems: The relevant plotted results do not provide exact values in the supplied text. The paper's main evidence concerns instability and loss behavior, not classification-error convergence; V5's cited catapult and long-run sharpness claims are not independently established here.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows were omitted. Cited results from Cohen et al. (2021) and Lewkowycz et al. (2020) were excluded because they are prior work, not this study's results.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error under the specified SGD/Adam recipes, including corrupted labels and model-size or regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of one or two additional student neurons.
Controlled depth comparisons, identity shortcuts, and the specified alternatives for training very deep networks.
Initialization comparisons, signal and gradient preservation, training speed, and trainable depth.

The complete wide-network squared-loss catapult sequence relative to the initial linearized stability limit, its larger-rate divergence boundary, and divergence despite initially subthreshold learning rates. Figure 33 changes the learning rate near convergence rather than testing the initial-training catapult recipe.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup training-speed or stability comparisons.

missing.what: Separate progressive sharpening, edge-of-stability training, and later sharpness decline into phase-specific results. The existing row records primarily the association between threshold crossings and loss increases.

The study's own MNIST four-layer MLP results show progressive sharpening and edge-of-stability behavior at learning rate 0.05, including little instability when the leading gradient projection is small despite above-threshold sharpness.

Near-converged VGG training on a 10,000-example CIFAR-10 subset with squared loss becomes unstable and exits the low-gradient region when the learning rate increases from 0.1 to 0.13. Record the authors' caveat that this only approximates a local-attraction test.
Reducing the learning rate from 0.05 to 0.01 during VGG full-batch CIFAR-10 training stabilizes training while sharpness increases.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any listed version. Exact numerical ordinates are unnecessary where the supplied text explicitly describes the observed behavior. Missing catapult evidence is untested scope, not grounds for a limits_scope verdict. Comparisons of principal-flow prediction accuracy and DAL performance do not independently test the listed claims.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 fit, random or corrupted labels, and effects of model size, early stopping, or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects on training error, identity shortcuts, special initialization for plain deep networks, and residual networks without normalization.
Initialization comparisons and their effects on training speed or trainable depth.

The paper studies instability around the 2/h threshold, but does not test the stated wide-network squared-loss catapult recipe or report its transient rise followed by low training loss. The sharpness and loss behavior over longer times is presented as figure-only evidence; no numerical values are recoverable from the text.

rows.subject: VGG
rows.operation_detail: Measured training loss, largest Hessian eigenvalue relative to 2/h, and loss-increase frequency during full-batch gradient descent.
rows.measure: Training loss and relationship of loss increases to whether λ0 > 2/h.
rows.note: The accompanying text says loss-increasing iterations overwhelmingly occur when λ0 > 2/h; the plotted values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: Figure 9 and Section 5 report progressive sharpening toward 2/h, edge-of-stability behavior, and predominantly above-threshold loss increases. The missing catapult experiment does not make this observed component partial. Cross-entropy sharpness decreases later in training. The loss/eigenvalue curves use learning rates 0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1 and 0.5; the loss-increase proportion panel uses 0.01 through 0.1.

source_check.locator_found: Figure 9, p. 13; Section 5 opening paragraph; appendix figure-reproduction entry for Figure 9.

rows.subject: VGG
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss-increase regions with the real part of the principal-flow stability coefficient for the leading eigendirection during gradient descent.
rows.measure: Training loss and Re[sc0] over training iterations.
rows.note: Text says loss increases are proportional to increases in the positive-gradient-flow behavior in the plotted region. This measures instability related to the threshold, but does not establish V5's catapult trajectory.
rows.check: Figure 13 uses ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 at learning rate 0.03, not VGG at 0.01. It plots actual gradient-descent loss and sharpness against 2/h alongside flow diagnostics. The observed instability is not partial merely because this experiment does not test the catapult sequence.

source_check.correct: Figure 13 uses ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 with learning rate 0.03. It plots loss, largest Hessian eigenvalue relative to 2/h, and Re[sc0], alongside negative and positive gradient-flow diagnostics. Values remain figure-only.
